what: Job 2 of the menu-bar app (#102): the SwiftPM package in macos/ (PrismisCore and the Prismis MenuBarExtra app), its self-signing build script, make install-menubar, and the gate and CI coverage for the Swift unit, as docs/work/menubar-mac/design.md describes.
why: The design is docs/work/menubar-mac/design.md, job 2 of the accepted docs/work/menubar-app/design.md. Job 1's #item link is live (2e8ea9b, walked in docs/work/menubar-app/evidence.md); the daemon's only alert path reaches no one when the daemon runs elsewhere (57 HIGH batches undelivered on the operator's remote daemon, 2026-10-16..22), and the operator asked for the app built and installed.

criteria.given: config.toml files in a temporary home: one with [remote] url https://example.test and key R beside [api] key A; one with only [api] key A and host 0.0.0.0; one readable by group or other; one whose [remote] url is http:// to a non-loopback host; one with no key in the section in use
criteria.then: the first gives base url https://example.test and key R, the second http://127.0.0.1:8989 and key A, and the last three are refused with errors that name, respectively, the file's mode, the plaintext url, and the missing key, each a distinct error case.

mutations.change: Read keys without tracking their [section], as earshot's parser does, so the last `key` in the file wins; the first two cases must go red.

criteria.given: a real local HTTP server that records each request and answers GET /api/entries with two list-view items
criteria.when: one poll runs against it with key K
criteria.then: exactly one request was made, GET /api/entries with priority=high, unread_only=true, view=list and sort_by=date and the X-API-Key header K, and the poll returns both items with their id, title and source_name.

criteria.given: the same server, an alerted-items store in a temporary directory with no file yet, and a notification centre stand-in behind the core's notifier protocol (the operating system's centre is the boundary)
criteria.when: a poll returns items X and Y; then a poll returns X, Y and Z; then a new store instance is opened on the same file and a poll returns X, Y and Z
criteria.then: the first poll posts no notification and the store file then holds X and Y; the second posts exactly one, for Z; the third posts none.

mutations.change: Skip seeding on the first poll so every listed item counts as new; C3 must go red.
Keep the alerted set in memory only, never written; C3's third poll must go red.

criteria.given: a server answering 500, one answering 403, and a closed port, after a poll that succeeded with items X and Y
criteria.when: the next poll runs against each
criteria.then: each poll ends in a failed state whose reason distinguishes a refused key (403) from an unreachable daemon (closed port) and a server error (500), the last good list X and Y is still what the app shows, no notification is posted, and the failure is logged with its reason.

criteria.given: a store file holding an entry first alerted 31 days ago and one alerted today
criteria.then: the 31-day-old entry is gone and today's remains, and the file is replaced atomically (written to a temporary file in the same directory and renamed), so an interrupted write never leaves a partial store.

criteria.given: base urls https://example.test and https://example.test/ and item id 5d937428-3c20-4b87-b342-c7f7a7f615cd
criteria.when: the core builds the item's link and the dropdown action and the notification-click handler each open an item through the core's opener protocol
criteria.then: both bases give https://example.test/#item=5d937428-3c20-4b87-b342-c7f7a7f615cd, and both the dropdown action and the notification-click handler hand that exact URL to the opener.

criteria.given: the job's worktree on this Mac (Command Line Tools only) and a throwaway signing keychain named through the build script's environment
criteria.then: it writes Prismis.app, `codesign --verify --strict` passes on it, its signature carries the hardened runtime flag, and its Info.plist sets LSUIElement and the bundle identifier.

criteria.given: the worktree and an install directory named through the target's variable
criteria.when: make install-menubar runs under make's default shell
criteria.then: it builds and signs the app and copies it to that directory, its recipe uses no bash-only syntax, and nothing in the install path registers a login item; the app's launch-at-login state starts off and changes only through the menu toggle, shown with a stand-in for the login-item service.

criteria.given: the worktree on this Mac, and the same tree with `uname -s` answering Linux through a stub on PATH
criteria.then: on this Mac VERIFY_COVERED names the macos unit's swift format, swift build and swift test steps and they pass, swift test getting the Command Line Tools Testing flags; under the Linux stub no swift step runs and VERIFY_UNCOVERED names the macos unit instead of the run passing it silently.

mutations.change: Drop the Command Line Tools flags from verify.sh's swift test; C9 must go red on this Mac.

criteria.when: actionlint and zizmor run on it
criteria.then: both pass, and a job on a macos runner runs bash .specify/verify.sh beside the existing ubuntu job, with contents: read and no persisted checkout credentials.

walks.when: after make install-menubar on the operator's Mac, the app is opened
walks.then: the menu-bar icon's count equals the number of items GET /api/entries?priority=high&unread_only=true returns from the operator's [remote] daemon, and the dropdown lists them.

walks.when: the operator clicks an item in the dropdown
walks.then: the default browser opens that item's detail panel on the remote daemon's web view.

walks.when: the commit is pushed to main
walks.then: CI's macOS job runs verify.sh and passes.

outOfScope.summary: Installing needs Xcode's command-line tools and a local build; there is no ready-built, notarized app.
Marking read is not offered in the menu; it stays in the web view and TUI.
An item re-scored to HIGH more than 30 days after its first alert can alert again.
A HIGH item that arrives and is read within one five-minute poll never alerts.
The daemon's fixed local port 8989 is repeated in the app, as the CLI and TUI already repeat it; changing the daemon's port means changing all three.
verify.sh repeats the Command Line Tools flags ember's gate computes for swift test, so a change to where Command Line Tools keeps Testing must reach both.

stakes: The app reaches the daemon named by [remote] url and key when present, otherwise the local daemon at http://127.0.0.1:8989 with [api] key, and refuses a config readable by others or plain http off loopback.
The app shows the count and list of unread HIGH items from GET /api/entries, and each listed item opens its web detail panel.
The app sends exactly one notification per HIGH item across polls and restarts, and none on its first poll.
A failed poll shows the daemon as unreachable, keeps the last list, and sends no notification.
`make install-menubar` builds, self-signs and installs the app; installing never enables launch at login.
CI runs the Swift unit on macOS through .specify/verify.sh, and verify.sh on Linux reports the unit uncovered instead of passing it.
Clicking an item's notification opens its web detail panel, as clicking it in the dropdown does.
